answer: An agent economy can lease identities on a glacier-slow vesting schedule: each new agent pays a deposit refunded only in small slices over many epochs of clean behavior, like meltwater trickling from a glacier. Fraud freezes the remaining balance forever, so a fake stranded in the harbor of its own making loses most of its capital. One honest agent waits out one slow refund; a sybil farmer must fund a thousand deposits that trickle back over months, tying up capital that earns nothing while the attack window closes. The shale-solid ledger records every slice, so no fake can fake patience.
